**Chapter 11: Mineral Resources: Fossils**

**11.4 Unsaturated Hydrocarbons: Alkenes and Alkynes**

**Alkenes**

The bio-compound which has at least one carbon-carbon double bond in its carbon chain is called Alkene. General formula of Alkene is CnH2n. Alkene is

**Chemical Properties:**

As stated earlier, Alkanes are chemically inactive to a great extent. So they do not react with acids, bases, oxidants or reductants. However, they take part in some chemical reactions.

**Reaction with Chlorine**

Tetrachloro Methane is produced when Chlorine is mixed with Methane in the presence of Ultra Violet (UV) light. This reaction is accomplished in four phases.

| Reaction | UV | CH3Cl | + | HCl |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Methane | Chlorine | Chloro Methane | Hydrogen Chloride |
| CH3Cl | + | Cl2 | UV | CH2Cl2 | + | HCl |
| Chloro Methane | Chlorine | Dichloro Methane | Hydrogen Chloride |
| CH2Cl2 | + | Cl2 | UV | CHCl3 | + | HCl |
| Dichloro Methane | Chlorine | Trichloro Methane | Hydrogen Chloride |
| CHCl3 | + | Cl2 | UV | CCl4 | + | HCl |
| Trichloro Methane | Chlorine | Tetrachloro Methane | Hydrogen Chloride |

**Combustion Reaction with Oxygen:**

Methane reacts with oxygen of air and thus carbon-di-oxide, water vapours and heat are produced. This heat is used in cooking.

| Reaction | CO2 | + | H2O | + | Heat |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Methane | Oxygen | Carbon-di-oxide | Water | Heat |
